findings.title: In-process manifest prune has no path-containment guard (port dropped it)
findings.description: The new `InstallManifest.finish()` prune loop computes `const file = path.join(this.targetRoot, rel)` for each stale `rel` read from the on-disk manifest (`oldLines.map(pathField)`), then `fs.rmSync(file)` when the file's CRC matches. `rel` is attacker/ user-controllable text: the module doc and the config key both treat `.context-forge/<target>.manifest` as a user-editable, guide-readable file, and a `pathField` value containing `..` (or an absolute path) makes `path.join` resolve outside `targetRoot`, so `isFile` + CRC-match + `rmSync` will delete a file outside the checkout. The pre-port cf `pruneStaleFiles` explicitly guarded this with `escapesLexically` / `isWithin` (realpath containment) and reported it as `reason: 'containment'` instead of deleting; that guard was not carried into the port. This is reachable in normal cf flow: worktree manifests are written by cf during worktree installs, so a user who edits a worktree manifest to add a `../<something>.md` entry gets that file deleted on the next `cf setup-ide`. Recommend adding the same lexical + realpath containment check before the `rmSync` and treating a violation as a "kept, warn" entry.

findings.title: `INSTALL_PATHS` list duplicated between source and test harness
findings.description: The top-level install-paths list (`CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.md.pre-context-forge`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md.pre-context-forge`, `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.github`, `.agents`, `MANIFEST_DIR`, `LINT_WRITE_PATHS`) is re-declared in `packages/cli/tests/ideInstall/harness.ts` under a different name but with identical semantics, because the snapshot's `installEntries()` walks exactly that list. The two copies are a manual-sync contract: adding a new top-level write target in `paths.ts`/`installer.ts` without mirroring it in `harness.ts` will silently stop showing up in snapshots and stop being compared by `dryRun.reportChanges`'s `before`/`after` sets, so a stale-file regression in that new path would not be caught. Consider exporting a single canonical list from `paths.ts` and having the harness import it.

findings.title: Verification summary
findings.description: Confirmed against source: (a) all re-exports from `setup-ide.ts` (`TARGETS`, `MANAGED_MARKERS`, `normalizeTarget`, `setupIdeAction`, `isManagedInstall`) still satisfy `init.ts` and the command registration; `worktreePropagation.ts` now only exports `propagationTargets` and no caller still imports the removed `propagateToWorktrees`/`pruneStaleFiles`/`sweepGeneratedPrompts`. (b) The new `SetupIdeRun` shape (`{ guideDir }`) is consistent with `installWorktrees` and the two worktree-loop tests; per-checkout `rules.exclude` is read through `ConfigManager(root)` for the main root and each worktree, which matches the bash `read_rules_exclude` contract and the new "reads rules.exclude for each worktree root" test. (c) `dryRunInstall` copies the install paths into a fresh `mkdtemp` sandbox, runs `installTarget` with `targetRoot: sandbox`, and cleans up in `finally`; the "removes the dry-run sandbox when the install aborts" test exercises the abort path (missing rules dir) and asserts no leftover. (d) `checkLintConfigs` runs inside `installTarget` after `manifest.finish()`, so lint-written files are not in the manifest and are not pruned — consistent with the test `test_lint_python_write_lint_writes_baseline` which runs `agents` (the target with the least output) and asserts `ruff.toml` content. (e) The `#40` getApplyTo fix (single `**` instead of `**\n**`) and the `#38` missing-final-newline preservation are mirrored by updated unit tests and by the regenerated snapshots; the `MANAGED_MARKERS` docstring in `ideTargets.ts` now correctly describes cf-installer-as-writer. (f) `parseRulesExclude` is exported from `@context-forge/core/node` and used consistently in the validator and in the CLI's `readRulesExclude`. The one behavioral regression worth fixing before merge is the manifest-prune containment drop noted above.
